core_fact: Microsoft has explicitly said generic Public Folder CRUD will not be added to Microsoft Graph. Programmatic Public Folder access therefore has no direct Graph replacement after EWS retirement.

demand_signals.signal: Generic Public Folder CRUD is explicitly listed among EWS capabilities that will not be added to Graph.
Public Folder backup and restore support stops as its Exchange backup moves from EWS to Graph.
Public Folder backup/restore becomes unsupported; recommends migration because no Graph API exists.
Public Folder protection continues only through temporary EWS transition; recommends shared mailboxes as replacement.
Customers using Public Folder contacts/calendars must migrate their sync source because third-party access will stop.
Product release notes explicitly warn that Exchange Online Public Folder access ends October 1, 2026.
Actively markets migration planning around the loss of programmatic Public Folder CRUD.
Published 2026 guidance specifically for Public Folder-to-shared-mailbox migrations and EWS transition configuration.
Actively markets Public Folder migration before EWS retirement.
Offers Public Folder Connector to shared mailboxes, SharePoint, M365 Groups/Teams and file targets; reports a live 17 TB PF-to-SharePoint migration.
SMB EWS retirement service treats Public Folder workflow discovery/migration as part of the operational project.
Explicitly frames Public Folder, archive and group gaps as urgent workloads for MSPs managing M365 migrations.

gate_result.result: The broader EWS/Public Folder ecosystem easily exceeds the threshold when vendor notices, migration guidance, backup deprecations and migration offerings are counted; at least 12 high-quality named signals are recorded here rather than padding the file with low-quality duplicates.
plausible_channels: IT providers with legacy Exchange customers

competitive_reframe.finding: Migration execution is already crowded. CodeTwo, BitTitan, AvePoint and ExchangeSavvy provide tooling or services. Building another migration engine would be poor capital allocation.
competitive_reframe.better_wedge: Vendor-neutral Public Folder Exit Planner: inventory + classify each folder by actual use + destination recommendation + dependency/backup risk + migration runbook + tool-neutral handoff.
why: The hard decision is not merely moving bytes; different Public Folders map naturally to shared mailboxes, M365 Groups, SharePoint/Teams, CRM, archive or deletion.
Existing migration vendors benefit when an assessment creates a clean migration specification, making them potential downstream channels rather than only competitors.
Assessment can be delivered without building a migration transport engine or retaining customer content.
The same inventory can identify EWS-dependent backup/sync integrations that otherwise fail after the cutoff.

offer.name: Public Folder Exit Planner
outputs: handoff specification compatible with third-party migration tools

next_gate.objective: Prove that the planner itself is useful rather than merely the underlying migration market.
next_gate.pass: Create a deterministic classifier and run it on >=20 synthetic representative Public Folder cases covering mail, contacts, calendars, documents, archives and mixed workflows; >=90% of cases should produce an explainable destination and flag ambiguous cases for human review.
next_gate.then: Only after the classifier works, consider a lightweight public Rockrai experiment; no domain purchase or paid promotion.
